summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of alcohol abuse, COPD, and recurrent pneumonia, was admitted after being found down following heavy alcohol intake. He presented with hypoxia, shortness of breath, and cough productive of green sputum. He was treated for pneumonia with Bactrim, guided by sputum culture showing Staph aureus sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and for alcohol withdrawal with high-dose diazepam. His oxygen levels improved, and he was weaned to room air. Despite refusing nebulizer treatments, his respiratory status stabilized. Due to his pattern of repeated admissions and incomplete treatment courses, a Section 35 was initiated, and he was discharged in police custody for admission to an alcohol treatment facility. He was medically stable at discharge, with plans to complete his antibiotic course and continue vitamin supplementation and blood pressure medications.
